newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia steps up "Supermarket to Asia" programme.
newsitem.headline: Australia steps up "Supermarket to Asia" programme.

text.p: Australia's "Supermarket to Asia" plan, a top-level government-industry programme which aims to boost processed food exports to the Asian region, saw significant value in niche markets, Australia's Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said on Wednesday.
The markets were small by Asian standards but of significant value to Australia, Anderson said in a statement.
Tuesday's federal budget allocated A$1.21 million to the project in new funding for 1997/98 as part of A$11.8 million allocated for the three years from 1996/97.

Seed capital of A$600,000 was allocated to assist the programme to start promotional activities in Asia in 1997 with industry taking over responsibility for promotional funding from the beginning of 1998.
The programme would undertake coordinated retail and food service promotions in Asian countries with Australian food companies, Anderson said.
It would promote a "Quality Food Australia" logo as a quality certification mark which would be available as an umbrella brand for Australian food in Asian markets, he said.
It would also establish a network of contacts throughout Asia which would assist current and new exporters with the development of their businesses, Anderson said.

In 1997/98 the Australian government would provide A$1 million under a programme to be known as "The Delicatessen" to help Australian food producers appreciate specific requirements of Asian customers and to enable them to capture export opportunities for high-value, niche market foodstuffs, he said.
